exact_archival_killer_question: Does the 1999 thesis or unpublished Bailey-Cameron-Papadopoulos manuscript contain an algorithm that partitions repeated/parallel generator columns into equivalence classes and optimizes coordinate order via per-class states equivalent to {not-started, active, finished}?

Does either source give a product state count equivalent to 2^s*3^r, an exact transition graph over class endpoints, or an O(k*3^k)-type exact trellis/pathwidth optimization where k is the number of distinct column/geometric classes?
If not, do they cite an earlier source that does?

known: First/last matroid bases for a fixed coordinate order determine minimal trellis layer sizes.
Coordinate permutation changes trellis complexity and optimizing the order is difficult in general.
Repeated generator columns are explicitly allowed/recognized in the code-matroid correspondence.
The Papadopoulos/Cameron line relates first/last bases to generalized Hamming weights.
not_located_in_accessible_material: O(k*3^k) exact coordinate-order/pathwidth DP by number of distinct geometric classes

no_redundant_work_rule: Do not spend further cycles on broad Google-style searches for Papadopoulos. Next evidence must come from thesis/manuscript retrieval, secondary citation tracing that reveals their contents, or external expert testimony.
